adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding abstract getShortcut makes pre-upgrade grant extensions throw AbstractMethodError during encoder postInit and abort the entire server startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` (line 33). In Java, adding an abstract method to an interface that existing classes implement will cause those implementations to fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError if they don't implement the new method. The DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() method iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls getShortcut() on each one. If any third-party or extension grant type factory exists that was compiled against the old interface (without getShortcut()), it will throw AbstractMethodError when postInit() calls factory.getShortcut(), potentially aborting server startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — Runtime grant discovery overwrites an existing shortcut without collision validation, so hot or concurrent deployments can silently reclassify already-issued token IDs.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java lines 108-118 (getShortcutByGrantType method), when a grant type is not found in the cache, it fetches the factory and directly puts the shortcut->grantType and grantType->shortcut mappings without checking if the shortcut already exists for a different grant type. The postInit method (lines 68-82) does validate for duplicates by comparing map sizes, but this runtime discovery path bypasses that validation. If a hot-deployed grant type has a shortcut collision with an existing grant, it would silently overwrite the mapping, causing already-issued tokens to be misclassified when decoded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — setFormParams leaves the cached grantType unchanged, so rewritten or delegated requests issue token IDs labeled with the pre-rewrite grant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that setFormParams() at line 105 only updates this.formParams but does not recalculate this.grantType. Since grantType is initialized in the constructor from formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE), if setFormParams is called with different form parameters containing a different grant_type, the cached grantType field will remain stale. This could cause token IDs to be labeled with the wrong grant type when requests are rewritten or delegated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding required getShortcut makes existing compiled grant providers fail with AbstractMethodError during encoder startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface without a default implementation. Java interfaces require all implementing classes to provide implementations for all abstract methods. Any existing third-party or custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the old interface version will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when the new `getShortcut()` method is called. The `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` method iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls `getShortcut()` on each, which would trigger this error for any legacy implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 — The SPI documents three-character shortcuts while the decoder accepts exactly two, so conforming extensions produce undecodable IDs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the SPI documents 'three-character shortcuts' but looking at the actual Javadoc in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java line 30-33, it says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' which is just a description/example, not a strict requirement. The actual implementations all use 2-character shortcuts (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', etc.) and the decoder in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider expects exactly 2 characters for grant type (characters 4-6 of the 6-character encoded context). The documentation saying '3-letters' is slightly misleading but all actual implementations use 2 characters consistently, so there's no actual bug - the system works correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:87 — Removing the public Context copy constructor breaks source and binary compatibility for grant extensions that clone request context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from lines 102-116 in OAuth2GrantType.java. This constructor was previously public and part of the API. If any external grant extensions were using this copy constructor to clone request context (which is a reasonable use case for extending OAuth2 grant types), their code would break after this change. This is a breaking API change that could cause compilation failures or runtime errors for existing extensions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1054 — Replacing UUID access-token jti values with prefix-colon-UUID values breaks consumers of the existing token and TOKEN_ID event shape without a compatibility path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows that token IDs are changing from plain UUIDs to a prefixed format (e.g., 'onrtac:UUID'). This is visible in TokenManager.java lines 1051-1055 where the token ID is now encoded via `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)` instead of just using `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`. The test file changes in AssertEvents.java confirm this by updating matchers from `isUUID()` to `isAccessTokenId(grantShortcut)`. This is a legitimate architectural concern - existing consumers expecting UUID-format token IDs will break. However, this appears to be an intentional design change rather than a bug, making it an important non-bug concern about backward compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:51 — Initial offline-access tokens are encoded as ONLINE because the online user session is inspected before it is replaced by the offline session.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that initial offline-access tokens are encoded as ONLINE because the online user session is inspected before replacement. However, looking at the diff, the code at line 51 in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java checks `userSession.isOffline()` to determine if it's an offline session. The diff doesn't show any evidence of a timing issue where an online session would be inspected before being replaced by an offline session. The finding makes an assumption about session lifecycle that isn't verifiable from the diff itself. The code simply checks the current state of the userSession - if it's offline, it returns OFFLINE; if it's transient, TRANSIENT; otherwise ONLINE. Without seeing the calling code's session management, we cannot verify this claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Grant shortcuts are accepted at arbitrary lengths even though the decoder requires exactly two characters, so a custom grant can emit IDs that cannot be decoded.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the postInit method at line 74 accepts grant shortcuts from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() without validating their length. However, in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() at lines 68-70, the decoder explicitly requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 characters (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType). If a custom grant implementation provides a shortcut that is not exactly 2 characters, the encoded token ID will have an incorrect format that cannot be properly decoded. The code lacks validation to ensure shortcuts are exactly 2 characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — Replacing formParams leaves the cached grantType stale, causing later token IDs to encode the previous grant.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the Context class has a grantType field that is initialized in the constructor from formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) at line 102. There's also a setFormParams method at line 105 that allows replacing formParams after construction. However, this setter does NOT update the cached grantType field. If setFormParams is called with different form parameters containing a different grant_type, the grantType field will still hold the old value from the original constructor call. This could cause token IDs to be encoded with the wrong grant type. The finding correctly identifies this as a potential bug where the cached grantType becomes stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher slices indices 3..5 and rejects equality, so it accepts access-token IDs carrying the wrong grant shortcut.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in AssertEvents.java lines 479-486, the matcher checks `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This logic is inverted - it returns false (match fails) when the grant shortcut EQUALS the expected value, and returns true when it doesn't match. The correct logic should be `if (!items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` to reject tokens with the wrong grant shortcut. Additionally, the substring indices 3..5 appear incorrect based on the encoding format shown in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java which shows the format as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2), so grant type should be at indices 4..6, not 3..5.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Making getShortcut mandatory couples every grant SPI to token-ID serialization and breaks existing third-party factories when post-init invokes the new method.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface now has a new method `getShortcut()` added without a default implementation. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the code iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each one. Any existing third-party implementation of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that doesn't implement this new method will cause a compilation error or AbstractMethodError at runtime. This is a breaking change to the SPI contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:87 — Removing Context's public copy constructor creates an unrelated source and binary compatibility break for grant extensions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of a public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` at lines 102-116 in OAuth2GrantType.java. This constructor was part of a public inner class in a public interface (OAuth2GrantType.Context). Removing a public constructor is indeed a source and binary compatibility break - any external code that called `new Context(existingContext)` would fail to compile or throw NoSuchMethodError at runtime. This is a legitimate API compatibility concern for extensions that may have used this constructor, though it's in server-spi-private which suggests it's internal API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — The fixed six-character parser contradicts getShortcut's documented three-character allowance, making the cross-SPI format contract unsafe to implement.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the Javadoc says 'three-character' shortcuts, but the actual Javadoc in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' - this is a suggestion, not a strict requirement. The parser expects 6 characters total (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType), and all the grant type shortcuts defined in the diff are exactly 2 characters (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'pg', 'rt', 'ro', 'te', 'ci', 'dg', 'pc'). The format is consistent: each component is 2 characters, totaling 6. There is no contradiction - the '3-letters' in the Javadoc appears to be a typo or approximation, but the actual implementation consistently uses 2-character shortcuts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57 — Reading grant type from an ambient ClientSessionContext attribute forces every token-minting path to seed a hidden key and already duplicates that responsibility across four unrelated callers.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the grant type is read from a ClientSessionContext attribute (line 57 in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider), and the diff shows this attribute being set in multiple places: OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java (line 109), TokenManager.java (line 248), PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java (line 82), ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java (line 134), and StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java (line 237). This is a legitimate architectural concern - the responsibility for setting this attribute is distributed across multiple callers, creating a hidden coupling. However, this is a design/architecture concern rather than a bug, as the code will function correctly when the attribute is set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Context duplicates grantType from mutable formParams while setFormParams updates only one copy, allowing the two representations to drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that grantType is initialized from formParams in the constructor (line 102: this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)), and setFormParams method (line 105-107) updates formParams but does NOT update grantType. This means after calling setFormParams with different form parameters, the grantType field will still hold the old value from the original formParams, causing the two representations to drift. This is a real consistency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84 — The encoder depends on a newly public mapper helper to determine token type, leaking mapper policy into the encoding layer.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real architectural concern in the diff. The method `getShouldUseLightweightToken` was changed from package-private to `public static` in AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java (line 84), and this method is now called from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java (line 55) to determine token type. This creates a coupling where the encoding layer depends on mapper implementation details. While not a bug (the code will work), it's a legitimate design concern about layer separation - the token context encoder now depends on a mapper class to determine token characteristics, which could be considered a violation of separation of concerns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/TokenContextEncoderProvider.java:35 — The decode API and its reverse registries have no production caller, leaving a substantial part of the framework as test-only dead code.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the decode API (getTokenContextFromTokenId) has no production caller and is 'test-only dead code'. However, this is a new SPI being introduced, and the diff shows it's a complete framework with encoding used in TokenManager.initToken(). The decode method is part of the public API (TokenContextEncoderProvider interface) designed for future use cases like token introspection or validation. New SPIs commonly introduce APIs that will be consumed by future features or external implementations. The finding incorrectly characterizes this as 'dead code' when it's actually a properly designed extensible interface. The test file demonstrates the API works correctly, which is appropriate for new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The context value object validates grantType twice but never validates rawTokenId, weakening the invariant at the new type boundary.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at AccessTokenContext.java lines 70-74, the constructor has: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); - This is clearly a copy-paste bug where grantType is validated twice with different error messages, but rawTokenId is never actually validated. The second check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"). This is a real defect that weakens the null-safety invariant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Making getShortcut abstract makes existing third-party grant factories throw AbstractMethodError during encoder postInit and abort server startup after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` (line 33-37). This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that don't implement this new method. When DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` (lines 68-73 in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java), any third-party factory without this method will throw AbstractMethodError, causing server startup failure. This is a real backward compatibility bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — postInit accepts shortcuts without validating non-null two-character format, so a provider can abort startup with an opaque NPE or mint token IDs that this decoder rejects.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the postInit method in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java (lines 63-82), the code iterates over OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls gtf.getShortcut() without any null check or validation. If a provider returns null from getShortcut(), the code would put null as a key in grantsByShortcuts map, which could cause issues. Additionally, there's no validation that shortcuts are exactly 2 characters as expected by the decoder in getTokenContextFromTokenId() which expects encodedContext.length() == 6 (2 chars each for sessionType, tokenType, and grantType). A malformed shortcut would cause token encoding/decoding to fail with confusing errors. This is a real validation gap in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:82 — Comparing only map sizes can miss balanced duplicate IDs and shortcuts, leaving inconsistent encode/decode mappings instead of failing startup.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a flaw in the validation logic at line 82. The code checks `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())` to detect duplicates, but this only catches cases where the total counts differ. If two different grant types have the same shortcut (e.g., grant A -> 'ab' and grant B -> 'ab'), the grantsToShortcuts map would have fewer entries (due to key collision), but grantsByShortcuts would also have fewer entries (shortcut 'ab' maps to only one grant). Similarly, if two shortcuts map to the same grant type, both maps could end up with the same size while still having inconsistent mappings. The validation would pass but encode/decode would be broken. A proper validation would need to check for duplicate values, not just compare sizes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — The duplicated grantType null check lets a null rawTokenId become the literal suffix "null", enabling malformed or colliding token IDs instead of rejecting the input.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at AccessTokenContext.java lines 70-74, the code has: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); followed by Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");. The second check incorrectly validates grantType again instead of rawTokenId. This means rawTokenId is never null-checked, and if null is passed, it would result in the string 'null' being appended to the token ID in encodeTokenId() method (line 107: ':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()). This is a real bug - a copy-paste error where the wrong variable is being checked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114 — The clear-text token-ID prefix exposes session persistence and grant-flow metadata to every bearer-token recipient and token-ID logging or tracing sink.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the token ID encoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() creates a prefix like 'onrtac:' that reveals session type (online/offline/transient), token type (regular/lightweight), and grant type. This is visible in the diff at lines 103-111 where the encoding concatenates these shortcuts. While this is intentional design (the PR adds this feature for observability/debugging), the security concern about exposing metadata to token recipients is a legitimate architectural consideration that a reviewer might raise. However, this appears to be the intended behavior of the feature, not an accidental exposure, so it's more of a design discussion point than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The matcher slices the wrong characters and rejects equality, so it accepts token IDs with an incorrect grant shortcut.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in AssertEvents.java:483, the matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)` but the comment says 'Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char' which would be index 4, not 3. Additionally, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the grant shortcut MATCHES, which is backwards - it should return false when it does NOT match. This inverted logic means the matcher accepts token IDs with incorrect grant shortcuts and rejects correct ones.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 — This broad catch passes on the NullPointerException caused by the uninitialized sessionFactory, so it never verifies the intended unknown-grant exception.

adjudication.rationale: The test method testIncorrectGrantType() is testing the provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() method with an invalid grant type shortcut 'ac'. Looking at the DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider code, getTokenContextFromTokenId() calls factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut() which returns null for unknown shortcuts, then throws IllegalArgumentException with message 'Unknown value ... for grant type'. The test catches RuntimeException which includes IllegalArgumentException. The sessionFactory is not used in getTokenContextFromTokenId() - it only uses the pre-initialized grantsByShortcuts map. The finding incorrectly claims there's a NullPointerException from uninitialized sessionFactory, but the test setup properly initializes grantsByShortcuts in the @Before method, so the intended exception path is actually being tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1053 — No test issues a real access token and decodes its jti, leaving session type, lightweight type, grant propagation, and SPI wiring for the new production path unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new TokenContextEncoderProvider SPI with DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider that encodes session type, token type, and grant type into access token IDs. While there is a unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java) that tests encoding/decoding logic in isolation, the finding correctly identifies that there's no integration test that verifies the full production path - issuing a real access token through TokenManager.initToken() and then decoding its jti to verify the context is correctly propagated. The unit test only tests the encoder with mocked factory data, not the actual integration with ClientSessionContext attributes, UserSessionModel states, and the real grant type factories. This is a legitimate gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:73 — Missing null-raw-token coverage lets the duplicated grantType check accept a null ID that encodeTokenId serializes as "null".

adjudication.rationale: Looking at AccessTokenContext.java lines 70-74, the constructor has: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); - The second check incorrectly validates grantType again instead of rawTokenId. This means rawTokenId can be null, and when encodeTokenId() is called, it would serialize 'null' as a string in the token ID. This is a real bug - copy-paste error where the variable name wasn't updated.
